convoLines.text: "Do you dream about before? Or is it all — this — now?"
"Look — Then it's not gone. Not really. Keep going back."
"Columbus, Ohio, always. Same dream: I'm walking home and the street keeps getting longer. I wake up tired, like I actually walked it."
"Still on what you dream about."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want? Just... be straight with me."
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Stanley is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
"I check the treeline every hour. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
"The fire feels smaller without Stanley. The rest of us will have to be bigger."
You show them Wild Strawberry — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"You talk to it -- the System. Have you ever asked? About the taken -- about Nada?"
"I see." They take a moment to think about your answer.

"It's my niece, Nada. Is napping in a pod somewhere, they say. Seven years old and napping. She was never boring. Some nights I dream about the pods -- rows of them, humming. I wake up and I can't tell if it was a dream or a broadcast.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Stanley owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Thanks for listening. Most people change the subject."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"About that question — What did you do for fun? Before. The thing you'd do on a perfect Saturday."
"The free things. Turns out they were the expensive ones."
Their friendliness thins — still there, just held at arm's length.
"Still on what you did for fun."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up? No time to waste."
"You want to know about that? Okay." "Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "I dreamed Stanley was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
"That's... pretty much all of it, honestly."
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
You show them Pawpaw — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"I could talk all day, but — go on. We'll talk more."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"About what happened to my taken kin — Have you heard anything? About the taken. The pods. Anything at all."
They nod. "Okay."
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"Still nothing on Nada. I told you about the pods -- I keep thinking about them. The humming. Some nights I'm sure it's a dream. Other nights I'm sure it's not."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Stanley always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
"We bury, we grieve, we keep going. There's no step four."
"Still on what's been happening."
You show them Pawpaw — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"This was good." They mean it.
"We never did finish talking about what's been happening — that was 8 days back. Still on your mind? 'I could talk all day, but — go on. We'll talk more.'"
"Come see what I found. You won't believe it."
Brunhilde shows you where they go to think. "Don't tell the others. Everyone needs one place."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on what's been happening."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Yeah? What's up?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "I'd follow you out past the treeline. Don't tell the others — they'd want to come too."
"Here's what it would take, if you want more than this: show up when it costs you something. That's the whole test."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Right. Go on, then."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"We never did finish talking about what was on their mind — that was 8 days back. Still on your mind? 'Forget I said anything. What did you want?'"
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up? …if that makes sense."
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Last time things were different. They always are." "You feel that? The air before a storm. That's the village right now."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"That's the whole of it. Sorry."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Anyway." A small smile.
"As I said — Still on what's been happening."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"...Actually, forget it."
"You said you dream about before. Every night — the only place it still exists. Is it still there?"
They nod. "Okay."
"Walk my trap line with me? Extra hands, extra eyes."
It's quiet at the trap line. Brunhilde doesn't say much. Sometimes that's the whole point.
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Still on that personal stuff."
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "You feel that? The air before a storm. That's the village right now."
"I wish there was more to tell. That's it."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"I should go. You know where to find me."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"I keep dreaming about rows of pods. Humming. Tell me I'm not the only one."
"Still nothing on Nada. I told you about the pods -- I keep thinking about them. The humming. Some nights I'm sure it's a dream. Other nights I'm sure it's not."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want? Forget it."
"Huh. Let me think about that." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Everyone's choosing sides and pretending they aren't. I hate it."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on what's been happening. That's still where we are."
"Okay. That's — I need a minute. A long minute."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Thanks for listening. Most people change the subject."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"This was good." They mean it.

deathBeat: d41: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Stanley Baker is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d41: 🕯️ Stanley Baker is dead — a hushwolf. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d41: The village's quarrel was with Stanley — and Stanley is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
recoverHome: d42: That night, they bring Stanley home. Nobody asks you to help carry; nobody has to. By morning the grave is dug by the fire, and the body is laid out beside it. The filling of it is yours.
vouch: d41: At the grave, Brunhilde, Atlas, Frieda and 5 more speak for Wanjiru — "Stanley trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
systemVoice: d43: ◈ AUDIENCE TRIAL — SYSTEM: "The audience wants an encore. A trial, then — smaller this time, but televised." Haul 1,000 kcal to the pantry within 3 days. Reward: integration, and a lesson.
